title: Curated preparation can shadow the only recoverable previous profile
suggestion: Before materializing a missing curated live directory, detect the install lock and `.install-previous` state. Either serialize with the installer and run the same recovery transition, or fail with a diagnostic requiring `plugin install` recovery. Keep the check curated-only so ordinary profile initialization remains unchanged.
rationale: Activation renames the old live directory to `.install-previous` before moving the staged directory into place (`apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:803-820`). If the installer stops in that interval, normal startup or config dump reaches this call with no live directory and materializes a fresh default profile without checking the lock or backup. A fresh probe preserved the user's patch only in `.install-previous`, created a live profile with `[]`, and then showed `runPlugin(..., ['install'])` failing on the new live profile's missing `pnpm-lock.yaml` while both directories remained. The retained profile is no longer automatically recoverable.

title: Mixed-profile npm fallback accepts different direct peer resolutions
suggestion: Before comparing runtime closures, require the root and installed npm resolutions to match in `packageKey`, `packageVersion`, `npmIntegrity`, and `snapshotKey`, mirroring the Git branch and `assertCuratedInstalledLocks()`; add a mixed-profile test whose extra dependency forces fallback and whose two candidate importer versions differ only by peer suffix.
rationale: A managed custom profile with extra dependencies makes `hasBindableInstalledLocks()` return false, so `createInstalledArtifactResolver()` uses this candidate-local npm path. Both locks are checked separately against the catalog, but only their transitive closures are compared; the direct candidate's peer-suffixed `snapshotKey` is not part of an empty closure. A fresh probe with root `plugin-a@1.0.0(peer@1.0.0)` and installed `plugin-a@1.0.0(peer@2.0.0)` was accepted. This contradicts the resolver's documented root/installed agreement and the shared policy path, whose focused test correctly rejects the same direct-resolution mismatch.

title: Canonical serialization accepts non-plain sparse and subclassed arrays
suggestion: Before mapping an array, require `Object.getPrototypeOf(value) === Array.prototype`, a dense own-index set, and no extra string or symbol properties; add regression cases for sparse and subclassed arrays.
rationale: The array branch returns before prototype and own-key validation. A fresh probe showed `canonicalBenchmarkJson(new Array(1))` and `canonicalBenchmarkJson([null])` both return `[null]`, while an `Array` subclass is accepted despite the public plain-JSON contract. File-backed callers currently receive dense ordinary arrays from `JSON.parse`, so this is a defensive public-helper gap rather than a currently exercised production path.
